title: Zip two lists into a map with a two-parameter merge lambda

blocks.text: A lambda with two or more parameters wraps them in parentheses, `(a, b) -> a + b`, and either declares every parameter's type or none of them. A `BinaryOperator<Integer>` is exactly such a two-parameter lambda.

Write `Zipper.zip(List<String> keys, List<Integer> values, BinaryOperator<Integer> merge)`. It pairs `keys.get(i)` with `values.get(i)` and returns the pairs as a map. When a key comes back a second time, its new value is combined with the one already in the map as `merge.apply(existing, incoming)`.
The two lists need not be the same length.

cases.says: Keys and values at the same position become the map's entries.
When one list is longer, its extra items are ignored instead of failing.
A repeated key merges its values with the lambda as merge(existing, incoming), not by overwriting.
Two keys with the same text are one key even when they are different String objects, so the map is looked up by equals, not by identity.
The merge lambda is called as merge(existing, incoming): the value already in the map comes first.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A two-parameter lambda such as a BinaryOperator wraps its parameters in parentheses, with every type declared or none.
